slot.brief: Solve an equation like sin θ = cos θ or a simple compound-angle equation and give the general solution.

verdicts.working: Write cosθ = sin(π/2−θ). Then sin3θ = sin(π/2−θ) gives 3θ = π/2−θ+2nπ or 3θ = π−(π/2−θ)+2nπ. Thus θ = π/8+nπ/2 or θ = π/4+nπ.

working:
$\cos\theta=\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)$.\n$3\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\theta+2n\pi\Rightarrow\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{8}+\dfrac{n\pi}{2}$.\n$3\theta=\pi-\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)+2n\pi\Rightarrow\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}+n\pi$.

Independent check: Write cosθ = sin(π/2−θ). Then sin3θ = sin(π/2−θ) gives 3θ = π/2−θ+2nπ or 3θ = π−(π/2−θ)+2nπ. Thus θ = π/8+nπ/2 or θ = π/4+nπ.
solution:
Using $\sin x=\sin y$ iff $x=y+2n\pi$ or $x=\pi-y+2n\pi$:
$$3\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta+2n\pi\quad\text{or}\quad 3\theta=\pi-\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)+2n\pi.
$$
Hence $\theta=\frac{\pi}{8}+\frac{n\pi}{2}$ or $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}+n\pi$, where $n\in\mathbb Z$.

draft.distractor_notes: B: Uses an incorrect period for the first family.\nC: Omits the second sine-equality family.\nD: Gives incorrect periods and shifts for the two families.
